response: The clinician assessment for acute chest syndrome (ACS) in febrile patients with sickle cell disease is not accurate enough. History and physical examination have limited value in defining which febrile patients require a chest X-ray (CXR). Due to the high mortality and morbidity associated with ACS, it is recommended that empiric CXR should be considered when evaluating a febrile patient with sickle cell disease, as ACS is common in these patients and can be grossly underestimated by evaluating physicians.
